S2.prop.shop_bench_23955.why: the black-capped man (S2.fig.shop_man_dark_cap_23963) sits facing east across the small table S2.prop.shop_small_table_23983, painted 0.3 m east of his bench: at their real sizes (a 0.9 m bench, a 0.6 m table) they stood inside each other; the bench turned north-south (a builder choice) and set 0.75 m west of the table's centre, its south end clear of the shop's corner post, so his feet go under the top (the casting agent's request)

S2.grd.bank_lines_top_28900.why: the two long lines at the top east of the 望火楼 built as a low raised bank (0.28 m) between them in the ground's heightfield (blender/canal_scene.py ground()), the reading of a raised bank or field edge; a path's two edges (the other reading) would be the same worn strip. sides.what: invisible walls round the painted area, one per side (edge:south, edge:east, edge:north, edge:west; the world page drops a side that is a seam with a loaded neighbour): the S3 seam at u 20500 (west), the silk's top edge (north), the S1 seam at u 29050 (east), the silk's bottom edge (south)
sides.why: outside the painted area the scroll paints nothing (north, south) or the neighbours stand (west: S3, east: S1, painted panels until they are built)

west_on_land.what: edge:west runs only along the S3 seam's land parts: the north strip from the built north bank top's seam point (149.37, 24.68) to the silk's top (147.06, 30.54), and the south bank from the silk's bottom (160.85, -4.39) to its shore's seam point (156.16, 7.49); across the river the shore walls and the boats' rails close the walk
west_on_land.why: S3's moored boats and S2's north-bank cargo boat run across the seam's water: a wall there would stand across their decks

east_all_land.what: edge:east runs the whole S1 seam (267.21, -4.39) to (290.62, 30.54): the east reach's water ends at the silk's bottom just west of it (266.98, -3.14), under the massive willow
east_all_land.why: no water is painted on the S1 seam (map: S2.water.bian_river_e's east end)

south_on_land.what: edge:south runs along the silk's bottom edge only where it is land: the south bank from the S3 seam to the spit's end (160.85 to 189.97, D -4.39), and the sliver of bank between the east reach's end (266.98, -3.14) and the S1 seam's foot (267.21, -4.39); between them the river runs off the silk into the mist (the middle and east reaches run on 16 m south under it)
south_on_land.why: the silk's bottom edge cuts the water from u 22680 to 28970: a wall across the water would stand across the boats' decks at the bottom edge (the second grain boat, the bottom boat, the mat-roofed boat)

north_whole.what: edge:north runs the whole silk's top edge (D 30.54); the north-bank buildings' backs run past it (choice depths) and close themselves
north_whole.why: nothing past the silk's top is painted; the far street and the top buildings end there

shore.what: edge:shore: invisible walls along every real shore as built (the river plan's north shore, the mapped south shores of the west and second reaches), 0.5 m pieces from 0.6 m below the water to 1.3 m above the bank (kit_boats.water_strip's), only inside the painted area; none along the middle and east reaches' run-on lines south of the silk or across the reaches' joins (water on both sides)
shore.why: nobody walks into the river; boats are boarded where their rails touch a bank (the page drops those pieces)
